item.research_question: How can the structural instability associated with the lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) in high-entropy hydroxides be mitigated to achieve high activity and long-term stability for industrial water oxidation?
item.material_system: Na-doped high-entropy layered double hydroxide (Na-HE LDH) with composition Na0.045-HE LDH containing Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Na; compared to pristine HE LDH (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu) and NiFe LDH
item.processing_route: One-step hydrothermal synthesis at 120 °C for 6 h using Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, Co(NO3)2·6H2O, Mn(NO3)2·4H2O, Cu(NO3)2·3H2O, NH4F, urea, and NaCl (0.045 mmol) as precursors on carbon cloth
item.test_conditions: Electrochemical testing in 1.0 M KOH (pH ~14) at ambient temperature; long-term stability in anion-exchange membrane electrolyzer (AEMWE) with 30 wt% KOH at 60 °C and ~500 mA cm⁻² for 2000 h
key_findings: Na-HE LDH achieved an overpotential of 176 mV at 10 mA cm⁻², which is 154 mV lower than pristine HE LDH (330 mV) and 145 mV lower than commercial IrO2 (321 mV).
The Tafel slope of Na-HE LDH decreased to 29.6 mV dec⁻¹, significantly lower than HE LDH (54.8 mV dec⁻¹) and IrO2 (64.4 mV dec⁻¹).
The specific activity of Na-HE LDH at η = 250 mV was 0.66 mA cm⁻², which is 11.00 times higher than that of pristine HE LDH (0.06 mA cm⁻²).
The turnover frequency (TOF) of Na-HE LDH at η = 250 mV was 0.052 s⁻¹, 14.4 times that of HE LDH (0.0036 s⁻¹).
The Na-HE LDH electrode pair operated continuously for 2000 h at ~500 mA cm⁻² in an AEMWE with only a 7% current density decay after 1000 h.
The Fe leaching rate in Na-HE LDH was 1.1%, significantly lower than 3.2% for HE LDH and 28.9% for conventional NiFe LDH.
The contact angle of Na-HE LDH was 15.59°, indicating superior hydrophilicity compared to HE LDH (139.53°).

The OER mechanism shifted from adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) in HE LDH to lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) in Na-HE LDH, confirmed by 18O isotope labeling showing high 16O18O product content.
item.mechanism: The introduction of low-valence, non-catalytically active Na ions creates oxygen non-bonding (ONB) states and induces oxygen vacancies. This shifts the electron removal source from the metal-oxygen bonding band to the oxygen non-bonding band during oxidation, preventing the reduction of M-O bond order and subsequent structural collapse. Additionally, Na anchors Fe sites and enhances M-O covalency, while the high-entropy matrix inhibits metal leaching and phase segregation.
item.limitations: The text notes that conventional LOM-based catalysts suffer from surface remodeling, metal leaching, and bulk phase collapse, which this study aims to solve but implies remains a general challenge for the field. The authors also mention that while Na-HE LDH maintains a crystalline structure, an amorphous layer of about 20 nm forms on the surface after stability testing.
item.future_work: The study offers a strategy for designing efficient and stable lattice oxygen catalysts and provides insights for developing catalysts capable of withstanding industrial hydrogen production environments, suggesting the approach can be applied to other high-entropy systems.

the introduction of Na facilitates the formation of oxygen non-bonding band thereby mitigating structural instability.
